sections.title: The letter té
paragraphs: The letter name is (té) /teː/. Its main sound appears in (tél) /ˈteːl/, which means winter. This letter has two sounds. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This consonant can be voiceless or voiced.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: Press your tongue tip firmly against the ridge behind your upper teeth. Stop the air completely for a brief moment. Release the tongue cleanly. For the main sound, keep your voice off. For the second sound, switch your voice on. A voiced sound makes your throat shake. Place your fingers on your throat to feel that buzzing vibration.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: In most positions, the letter keeps its standard sound. You hear this in (torta) /ˈtortɒ/. A sound change happens before certain consonants. The voice switches on before a following voiced consonant. You hear this voiced sound in (hatvan) /ˈhɒdvɒn/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: In English, words like top have a puff of air. Hungarian plosives have no puff of air. Hold your hand before your mouth. Say the sound cleanly without any breath. Do not pull your tongue back into the mouth like in English tea.
